title: The memory test: ten questions after 12 months of ads
hook: A year of ads is research you have already paid for.
caption:
A year of ads is research you have already paid for.

Most teams can quote last month's RoAS. Fewer can say why their strongest ad did well, or which ads they would never run again.

Here is a test for your next review. Ten questions, laptops closed, 30 minutes. Each person writes their answers alone, then the room compares.

Seven or more answers that everyone agrees on: your brand remembers. Fewer than that: the learning is sitting in the ad account and in one or two heads.

The ten questions are in the slides. The December review is a good time to run it, while the sale is still fresh.

slides.headline: A year of ads. *Ten questions* your team should answer without a dashboard.
Laptops closed. *Write alone.* Then compare.
slides.body:
Give everyone the ten questions on paper.

Ten minutes to write. Twenty to compare.

An answer counts only when the room agrees on it and someone can name the ads behind it.

slides.headline: What *worked*, and for whom
items: Which opening shots held attention longest this year?
Which buyer was each of our strongest ads speaking to?
How many weeks does a strong ad last before it tires?
Which format suits which product in our range?
Which offer brought buyers back for a second order?

slides.headline: What to *stop*, and what comes next
items: Which ads only did well during a sale?
What do creator videos do for us that studio shoots do not?
Which message have we repeated most, and is it still paying?
Which ads would we never run again, and why?
What is the first thing we test next quarter?

slides.headline: What the score *tells you*
left: Put the answers in every brief
Run the test again each quarter
right: The learning lives in a few heads

slides.headline: Plenty of data. *No memory.*
slides.sub: The questions your team disagrees on are your test plan for next quarter.

slides.headline: Take the ten questions into your *next review*
slides.sub: Save this post so you have them in the room.

notes:
Hook shape: punchy plus context. Reader: a D2C founder or CMO running the December review after the sale season. Argument: test whether your team can recall what a year of ads taught it, without a dashboard. No statistics used; '30 minutes', 'ten questions' and 'seven' are the test's own rules.
